verdict.rationale: Unity documents a first-party Unity CLI for installing and managing Editors and modules, aimed at scripts, automation and CI. A runtime probe verified a keyless install script, JSON/TSV output, documented exit codes, a CLI llms.txt, and `unity <command>`/`unity eval` commands that drive the Editor directly for agents that can run shell commands. Editor command-line arguments for headless automation add to this. Missing for 10: the CLI is still labelled experimental, and there is no independent or community hands-on corroboration of agent use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: Use the Unity CLI to install and manage Unity Editors and modules from the command-line
The Unity CLI works well for: Continuous integration (CI) and build agents where installing the full Hub is undesirable.
Unity now ships a first-party standalone CLI (experimental) with a public keyless install script
structured JSON/TSV output and documented exit codes
You can launch the Unity Editor and Player with additional command line arguments to control startup behavior, configure settings, or automate workflows.
